documents.title: Academic Policies: Artificial Intelligence and Generative AI section
documents.summary: The student policies page tells students that instructors decide whether AI is allowed, that they must check each syllabus, acknowledge permitted AI use, and verify AI output. Improper use counts as academic misconduct.
documents.stance_why: The section says "Instructors have the right to specify if, when, and how AI may be used in their classes" and sends students to each syllabus, so it sets no stance of its own.

units.why: The opening sentence frames AI as "rapidly changing" with "new opportunities and challenges", a principle that frames the whole section, so it is a framework statement (P56) addressed to all.
units.anchor: generative artificial intelligence is a rapidly changing technology that is creating both new opportunities and

units.why: "Transparency and accountability are expected" is a general expectation on all users of generative AI; it is a principle rather than a specific disclosure rule, so it fits the institution-wide framework P56 better than P24, which the later acknowledgment sentence carries.
units.anchor: Transparency and accountability are expected with the use of generative AI.

units.why: "Instructors have the right to specify if, when, and how AI may be used in their classes" hands the decision to each instructor, matching P04; the actor is the student because it tells students who decides.
units.anchor: Instructors have the right to specify if, when, and how AI may be used in

units.why: "You should always check every syllabus" puts on students the duty to find and follow the course-level AI rules, which is P78; P10 (ask when unsure) is carried by the next sentence.
units.anchor: You should always check every syllabus for clarification and policies

units.why: "Contact your instructor if that information is not available in the syllabus" tells unsure students to ask the instructor, which is exactly P10.
units.anchor: Contact your instructor if that information is not available in the syllabus.

units.why: "students will provide appropriate acknowledgment of their AI use" when AI is allowed is a disclosure expectation (P24); the comparison to citing sources is noted but the core rule is acknowledgment.
units.anchor: students will provide appropriate acknowledgment of their AI use
units.frag_end: in classroom work, research, or academic writing
units.policy: When AI is allowed, students are expected to provide appropriate acknowledgment of their AI use, just as UNLV requires appropriate citations and references for any sources used in classroom work, research, or academic writing.

units.why: "expected to check any information generated by an AI platform for inaccuracies, as generative AI can produce incorrect information" is the verify-output rule P31.
units.anchor: expected to check any information generated by an AI platform for inaccuracies

units.why: "is a form of academic misconduct and subject to student sanctions" classifies improper AI use, as defined by the integrity policy or the instructor, as misconduct, which is P36.
units.anchor: is a form of academic misconduct and subject to student sanctions

documents.title: Instructor Requirements and Resources: Artificial Intelligence and Generative AI section
tiers: Use is freely permitted with no acknowledgment
documents.summary: The instructor page requires faculty to state their AI rules in the syllabus at the start of the course and update them. It lists questions for drafting a statement and four sample statements ranging from free use to a ban.
documents.stance_why: It repeats that students "should contact their instructors for clarification" and gives instructors sample syllabus options from "Use is freely permitted" to "Use prohibited", so the stance is left to instructors.

documents.title: AI Best Practices
documents.summary: UNLV IT states that no AI-specific campus policy exists and that existing policies apply. It gives practices on disclosure, data privacy, third-party tools, bias and verifying outputs.
documents.stance_why: The page says "There is no specific AI policy currently on campus" and gives conditional best practices (acknowledge use, protect data, verify output), so it permits AI with conditions rather than setting a campus rule.

units.why: "There is no specific AI policy currently on campus, however, existing university policies already encompass the use of AI technologies" says AI use falls under existing policies, which is P77.
units.anchor: existing university policies already encompass the use of AI technologies
units.fit_note: Also states that no AI-specific policy exists at UNLV.

units.why: "required to adhere to NSHE and institutional policies and procedures" binds users to existing rules: P77.
units.anchor: required to adhere to NSHE and institutional policies and procedures

units.why: "no UNLV-wide policies have been outlined relating to AI assessment, grading, content creation, or general use" states that no campus rule exists on these matters, an institution-level scope statement; nearest is P56, though it describes absence.
units.anchor: no UNLV-wide policies have been outlined relating to AI assessment, grading, content creation
units.frag_start: It is important to note that
units.fit_note: Describes the absence of a campus-wide framework rather than stating one.

units.why: "Generative AI should be treated analogously to assistance from another person" treats AI as a human collaborator under existing rules: P45.
units.anchor: Generative AI should be treated analogously to assistance from another person.

units.why: "Examples of usage could be for drafting a professional sounding email or documenting some code" gives permitted example uses. Chosen P91 because drafting an email is writing support; P16 does not fit since no AI-generated code submission is described.
units.anchor: drafting a professional sounding email or documenting some code
units.fit_note: Also covers documenting code, not only writing support.

units.why: "Using generative AI tools to complete a Financial or Human Capital Management project ... is not advisable" is operational guidance about university administrative systems: P76.
units.anchor: Using generative AI tools to complete a Financial or Human Capital Management project
units.policy: Using generative AI tools to complete a Financial or Human Capital Management project is not advisable.

units.why: "entering assignment or exam answers is not advisable" discourages putting assignment or exam answers into AI, i.e. P20 (not feeding assignments to AI), though stated as advice not a ban.
units.anchor: entering assignment or exam answers is not advisable
units.fit_note: Worded as 'not advisable', not a prohibition.

units.why: "Personally identifiable information, system credentials ... and non-public records should not be provided as prompts" protects data: P50.
units.anchor: should not be provided as prompts
units.policy: Personally identifiable information, system credentials (passwords, IP addresses), and non-public records should not be provided as prompts.

units.why: "One should acknowledge the use of generative AI (other than incidental use) and default to disclosing such assistance when in doubt" is a disclosure rule with an incidental-use exemption: P24.
units.anchor: One should acknowledge the use of generative AI (other than incidental use)
units.fit_note: Exempts incidental use and says to disclose when in doubt.

units.why: "Avoid inputting sensitive or personal information into AI systems" is the data-protection advice P50.
units.anchor: Avoid inputting sensitive or personal information into AI systems.
units.fit_note: Also says to anonymize personal data and not use institutional data.

units.why: "Restrict the permissions granted to AI applications to only what is necessary" is a security least-privilege practice: P50 (protect data) is the nearest.
units.anchor: Restrict the permissions granted to AI applications to only what is necessary
units.fit_note: Concerns app permissions rather than personal data.

units.why: "Contact UNLV IT if needing to integrate AI into university applications to ensure compliance" routes integrations through IT review: P65.
units.anchor: Contact UNLV IT if needing to integrate AI into university applications

units.why: "Review AI outputs for malicious content, appropriateness, accessibility, bias or discriminatory outputs" is output checking: P31.
units.anchor: Review AI outputs for malicious content, appropriateness, accessibility, bias or discriminatory outputs.

units.why: "Always employ human judgment when using AI outputs" keeps humans in the decision role: P32.
units.anchor: Always employ human judgment when using AI outputs

units.why: "Enterprise tools are ... supported by UNLV ... Supported tools include data agreements and other protections for institutional data" defines the university-supported tool category and its protections: P92 as informing.
units.anchor: Supported tools include data agreements and other protections for institutional data and content.
units.fit_note: Defines enterprise vs third-party tools rather than directing use.

units.why: "When using third-party non-UNLV supported tools, it is imperative that you" review privacy policies: P50 (vetted tools, data protection).
units.anchor: Review their privacy policies
units.policy: When using third-party non-UNLV supported tools, it is imperative to review the AI tool's privacy policies to know how data will be used, stored, and protected.

units.why: "Check security measures: Ensure the tool has robust security measures in place, such as encryption" is vetting a third-party tool: P50.
units.anchor: Ensure the tool has robust security measures in place, such as encryption and secure data

units.why: "Limit data sharing: Only provide the minimum necessary data to the AI tool" is data minimization: P50.
units.anchor: Only provide the minimum necessary data to the AI tool

units.why: "Users are ultimately responsible for verifying the output they utilize from AI is free of discrimination, bias" assigns responsibility for checking bias and fairness: P31 (verify output), with bias concerns P53.
units.anchor: Users are ultimately responsible for verifying the output they utilize from AI is free of
units.frag_start: Users are ultimately responsible for verifying
units.fit_note: Concerns fairness and compliance with UNLV and NSHE policies, not only accuracy.

units.why: "AI models can output biased or discriminatory results" names bias as a harm: P53.
units.anchor: AI models can output biased or discriminatory results

units.why: "it is up to the user to verify the accuracy of the AI outputs" and AI "can also provide inaccurate or misleading information" is the verify-output rule: P31.
units.anchor: it is up to the user to verify the accuracy of the AI outputs

notes: No school or computing policy was found. IT page is guidance, not policy; coded as permit with conditions. The instructor and student pages repeat the same AI paragraph; each coded separately. Coder B.
